headline: Medibank CEO highlights premium cost pressure, payout ratio and value initiatives as key consumer metrics

I would say, though, that we are seeing the rise of aggregators in the market. The cost of aggregators, uh, in the industry has almost doubled in two years, and I think consumers deserve options to and we would promote choice and comparison. But unfortunately, the only true source of comparison is the government's website. Aggregators do not feature all funds or all products. And so, you know, this cost has been growing in plain sight. headline: Airlie's Vinay Ranjan sees Medibank as attractive investment opportunity trading below long-term P/E average with regulatory fear creating entry point
reasoning: Medibank, Australia's largest private health insurer with 4.2m members and 27% market share, has come under regulatory scrutiny amid a hospital sector lobbying campaign, creating what Airlie sees as a buying opportunity. The company screens as high quality: strong capital ratio of 14.1% (well above its 10-12% target) with zero debt, scale advantages that help negotiate better hospital terms and manage claims inflation, and experienced management under CEO David Koczkar since 2021 who has delivered policyholder growth and EPS growth of 8% p.a. over the past decade. Medibank has returned $1.46bn in COVID givebacks, keeping gross margins below FY19 levels, countering the narrative that it has profited at hospitals' expense. From a valuation perspective, Medibank trades on less than 17x P/E versus its long-term average of 19x, with a dividend yield of 4.6%, while regulatory risk appears overstated given the government's own health minister has acknowledged there is no silver bullet funding solution from Canberra.
quote: While there remains uncertainty as to how the regulatory situation will unfold with a federal election coming up, we think it's unlikely the government will step in and prop up private hospitals where there is a clear shift to lower-cost care outside the hospital. In the meantime, we believe this creates an opportunity to invest in Australia's largest health insurer, which has grown its earnings per share at 8% p.a. over the past decade. Medibank screens as a high-quality business under our investment process for the following reasons: 1) Financial strength: Medibank has a strong capital position with a capital ratio of 14.1%, well above its 10-12% target range, and has zero debt on its balance sheet. 2) Business quality: Medibank is Australia's largest health insurer with 4.2m members (27% market share). This scale enables Medibank to negotiate better terms with hospitals keeping a lid on claims inflation while sharing these savings with members to lower premiums and improve retention. 3) Management quality: David Koczkar has been the CEO since 2021 and prior to this was the COO since 2014. Over this period, the company has seen a return to policyholder growth, expanded its health offering and tightly managed its costs. Finally, from a valuation perspective, Medibank is trading on less than 17x P/E (below its long-term average of 19x) and offers investors an attractive dividend yield of 4.6%.
